key_insight: MORTIS gives a discrete theory for choosing quadrature-compatible cofactor gauges that preserve the full finite-element elasticity tangent while certifying optimal material margins in finite elasticity.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps build mechanically certified constitutive formulations and mesh-level coercivity guarantees without changing the assembled equations, which is valuable for robust nonlinear solid simulations.
method: Derive exact local potential spaces for several finite-element families, including tensor, anisotropic, serendipity, and tetrahedral elements.
Formulate a convex quadrature-point margin objective and prove when its optimum matches compatibility of the physical identity potential.
Use Gram-identity and curvature-based examples to quantify strict margin loss and certify when reference-defect-corrected gauges preserve the tangent.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical proofs, sharp constants, and certified examples/counterexamples rather than a primarily data-driven evaluation.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on explicit assumptions about space choice, quadrature, material coefficients, shape regularity, and boundary conditions, so compatibility may fail outside those settings.
paper_title: MORTIS: Quadrature-compatible cofactor gauges and optimal material margins in finite elasticity
